# Decision on the admissibility of a booking record

The appellant ⟦PERSON|Sola Merrowick⟧ challenges the exclusion of a booking record in proceedings against ⟦ORG|Tidal Acorn Travel Ltd⟧. The appeal concerns authenticity rather than the merits of the underlying cancellation dispute. The panel has inspected the exported message and the supporting transmission log.

The original record contains a contact block formatted as follows:

<div class="booking-contact">
<strong>Passenger:</strong> <span>⟦PERSON|Sola Merrowick⟧</span><br>
<strong>Home:</strong> <span>⟦ADDRESS|Unit 6, 92 Fable Street, Exeter⟧</span><br>
<strong>Email:</strong> <span>⟦EMAIL|sola.merrowick@tidal-acorn.invalid⟧</span>
</div>

The first instance decision treated the absence of a visible signature as decisive. That approach gave insufficient weight to the sequence of messages acknowledging the booking. The respondent's own export contains the same acceptance time and the same fare. There is no evidence of an intervening amendment.

We therefore admit the record and remit the remaining issues for determination. Admission does not establish that the cancellation term was incorporated or that the appellant accepted the proposed substitute journey. Those questions require findings on evidence that the panel has not heard.

Each party will bear its own appeal costs. Any application about transcription errors must identify the passage concerned and the wording sought. This decision was issued in Exeter on 7 November 2026.

Panel chair: ⟦PERSON|Fenla Ruskett⟧.
